name: Herod Agrippa I
title: Persecutor of the Early Church
summary: Herod Agrippa I was the grandson of Herod the Great and ruled over Judea from 41-44 AD. He was the first king to actively persecute the Christian community, killing the apostle James and imprisoning Peter. His sudden and dramatic death is described as a divine judgment because he accepted the people's worship.

keyEvents.title: Kills the Apostle James
keyEvents.description: Herod Agrippa I had the apostle James, the brother of John, executed by the sword. This was the first martyrdom among the twelve apostles.

keyEvents.title: Imprisoning Peter
keyEvents.description: When Herod saw that the execution of James pleased the Jews, he also had Peter arrested and imprisoned under strict guard.

keyEvents.title: Peter's Miraculous Release
keyEvents.description: An angel freed Peter from prison during the night, despite the sixteen soldiers who were guarding him.

keyEvents.title: Execution of the Guards
keyEvents.description: When Herod discovered that Peter was gone, he interrogated the guards and ordered them to be executed.

keyEvents.title: Herodes' Death as Divine Judgment
keyEvents.description: During a speech in Caesarea, the people shouted that it was the voice of a god. Because Herod did not give glory to God, he was struck by an angel of the Lord and died, eaten by worms.
